identity.name: Travis R. McKinzie
identity.headline: Web Solutions Lead & IT Professional — Cognitive Psychology, Digital Ergonomics, Human-Centered Systems
identity.summary: I design and build web systems that respect how people actually think and work. My background pairs a psychology degree with business administration and hands-on IT operations, and I apply that mix to web design, digital ergonomics, and automation: interfaces that reduce cognitive load, documentation people can find, and tooling that removes friction instead of adding it. This site is both my working notebook and a live demonstration of that approach — a static site generator I built to publish a personal knowledge base as a navigable, themeable, accessible website.

projects.name: This site — a personal knowledge base as a website
projects.description: A Python static-site generator that turns an Obsidian vault into a public digital garden: typed note cards, backlinks and a knowledge graph, four switchable themes, keyboard navigation, and a build that fails loudly on unsafe input. You are looking at the output.

projects.name: Claude Docs MCP Server
projects.description: A local Model Context Protocol server that gives coding agents search and discovery over a documentation corpus, so answers come from the docs rather than memory.

projects.name: Agent Mission Control
projects.description: A Next.js dashboard for tracking AI agents, goals, and runs across a personal tool ecosystem, connected to the knowledge base through an MCP seam with a strict one-owner-per-datastore rule.

projects.name: PDF Chunker
projects.description: Splits large PDFs into per-chapter files by detecting document structure, built to make long technical references usable in AI research workflows.

projects.name: File Sorter
projects.description: A small Python command-line tool for rule-based file organization — the kind of quiet automation that removes a daily chore.
